title: How do we say eight big numbers in words?
description: Kavya writes eight kilometre readings of school buses on a board in Mysuru. The video says each number's name, thousands part first.
teaching_notes: One idea: say the part before the comma and the word thousand, then the last three digits. Watch for a zero place: no word is said for it.

source: Let Us Do 2, write the names
video_script.why: The child can name one five digit number at a time but needs a steady way to name many, including those with zeros.
video_script.substitution: Say the part before the comma, then thousand, then the last three digits; leave out any place that holds a zero.
video_script.anchor: Kavya's list of bus readings on a school board in Mysuru
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu drops the word hundred in seven thousand two hundred nine. The zero is not said, but two still means two hundred.
video_script.payoff_line: say the thousands part, then the rest, and leave out any zero place

final_answer.value: 7,209 seven thousand two hundred nine; 10,599 ten thousand five hundred ninety-nine; 13,579 thirteen thousand five hundred seventy-nine; 45,045 forty-five thousand forty-five; 39,593 thirty-nine thousand five hundred ninety-three; 50,005 fifty thousand five; 26,050 twenty-six thousand fifty; 81,200 eighty-one thousand two hundred
final_answer.spoken: seven thousand two hundred nine, ten thousand five hundred ninety nine, thirteen thousand five hundred seventy nine, forty five thousand forty five, thirty nine thousand five hundred ninety three, fifty thousand five, twenty six thousand fifty and eighty one thousand two hundred

maths_rules: the part before the comma is said first with the word thousand; then the last three digits are read as hundreds, tens and ones
10,599: ten thousand five hundred ninety nine
13,579: thirteen thousand five hundred seventy nine
39,593: thirty nine thousand five hundred ninety three
a zero place is not said, but a digit before the zeros still names its place: 209 is two hundred nine
